memories.memory_text: I had a raw and painful conversation with Emery Everett where we both confronted how much we’ve lost—our son, our marriage, everything—and I told her I went back to smuggling because it was the only thing I was ever good at, while she insisted we could still save Nico Carter.

grounded_facts: A pivotal emotional encounter between Owen Adler and Nico Carter on a catwalk in the Oscillator Structure, witnessed by Carson Nolan, Owen Finch, and Cameron Sinclair.

Owen Adler confronts Nico Carter with truth and love, urging him to leave the Northstar Collective and return home, appealing to familial bonds.
memories.memory_text: I moved closer to Kylo on the bridge and told him that Evan Carter is using him for his power and will crush him when he's no longer useful, then urged him to leave with me and come home because we miss him.

grounded_facts: Nico Carter expresses emotional turmoil and a desire to be free from pain, showing genuine hesitation and vulnerability in the face of Owen Adler's appeal.
memories.memory_text: I saw Kylo hesitate and realized he knew the truth, and for the first time, I saw real conflict in him—tears in his eyes—and I heard him say he's being torn apart and wants to be free of the pain.

grounded_facts: In response to Nico Carter's plea for help, Owen Adler affirms his unconditional support.
memories.memory_text: I heard my son ask me for help, trembling with doubt, and I told him yes—anything—he could count on me.

memories.memory_text: I saw Nico Carter slowly extend his unlit the weathered jacket toward me, close enough that I could feel its weight in the air, and in that moment, I believed he was asking for my help, that he still had a chance to come back.

Nico Carter ignites his the weathered jacket through Owen Adler's chest, killing him, after Owen Adler reaches toward the offered weapon; Owen Adler falls from the catwalk into the depths.
memories.memory_text: I reached for the the weathered jacket, hoping it meant he was coming back to me, but then I saw the darkness in his eyes — he ignited it through my chest, and I felt myself falling, slipping away as I looked into my son's face one last time.

grounded_facts: A private, emotionally charged encounter between Owen Adler and his son Nico Carter atop the catwalk of the oscillator structure, culminating in Owen Adler's death.
memories.memory_text: I stepped toward my son, saw him extend his the weathered jacket toward me, and in my last moment, I looked into his face before falling from the catwalk.

Owen Adler chooses to reveal himself to Nico Carter instead of escaping, driven by emotional conflict and Emery Everett's words.
memories.memory_text: I saw Owen Adler step out onto the catwalk instead of escaping, and I heard him call out 'Nico Carter!' to Nico Carter, trying to reach the person he used to be.

grounded_facts: In response to Owen Adler's plea, Nico Carter takes off his mask, revealing his face.
memories.memory_text: I saw Nico Carter take off his mask and reveal his face when Owen Adler was pleading with him.

grounded_facts: Nico Carter claims that Owen Adler's son is gone and that he destroyed him.
memories.memory_text: I heard Nico Carter tell Owen Adler that his son was gone and that he had destroyed him.

grounded_facts: Owen Adler emotionally acknowledges Nico Carter as his son despite the latter's denial.
memories.memory_text: I saw Owen Adler refuse to believe Nico Carter's denial and insist that his son was still alive.

grounded_facts: Nico Carter is visibly weakened and horrified by a dark action he has committed, marking a moment of internal shock and physical vulnerability.
memories.memory_text: I saw Nico Carter looking horrified and weakened after what he'd done, like he was shocked by his own actions.

grounded_facts: Cameron Sinclair fires at Nico Carter in a furious retaliation after being wounded or provoked.
Cameron Sinclair, in agony and fury, fires at Nico Carter, hitting him in the side and causing him to fall back stunned.
memories.memory_text: I saw Cameron Sinclair fire at Nico Carter in fury, hitting him in the side and making him fall back stunned.

grounded_facts: Nico Carter sees and recognizes Owen Finch and Carson Nolan watching the explosions, reacting with astonishment before advancing toward them.
After rising from being stunned, Nico Carter sees Owen Finch and Carson Nolan, recognizes them with astonishment, and begins moving toward them aggressively.
memories.memory_text: I saw Nico Carter rise up and look right at Owen Finch and me, recognizing us with shock, and then he started coming toward us fast, and I knew we had to get out of there.

grounded_facts: Carson Nolan wraps his arm around Owen Finch and drags or carries her out of sight to protect her from incoming blaster fire.
memories.memory_text: I wrapped my arm around Owen Finch and dragged her out of sight to keep her safe from the blaster fire.

grounded_facts: Northstar Collective open fire on Owen Finch and Carson Nolan; Owen Finch fires back chaotically while Carson Nolan pulls her to safety, removing her from sight.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Northstar Collective opening fire on us, and I watched Owen Finch shoot back wildly while I pulled her to safety and got us both out of sight.

grounded_facts: Owen Finch and Carson Nolan stop fleeing upon realizing they cannot escape by running.
memories.memory_text: I stopped running because I realized Owen Finch and I couldn't escape by fleeing anymore, and she saw it too.

grounded_facts: Nico Carter uses the Force to disarm Owen Finch and throw her into a tree, causing injury and dazing her.
memories.memory_text: I saw Owen Finch try to shoot Nico Carter, but he used the Force to rip the blaster from her hand and throw her into a tree—she slammed into it hard and fell, dazed and hurt.

grounded_facts: Nico Carter declares that the weathered jacket belongs to him after seeing Carson Nolan wield it.
memories.memory_text: I ignited the weathered jacket, and when Nico Carter saw it, he shouted that it belonged to him.

grounded_facts: During the duel, Carson Nolan successfully blocks and counters Nico Carter's attacks, managing to graze Nico Carter's arm with the weathered jacket.
memories.memory_text: I blocked Nico Carter's attacks and actually managed to land a hit, grazing his arm with the the weathered jacket.

grounded_facts: After overpowering Carson Nolan in combat, Nico Carter strikes Carson Nolan and knocks the weathered jacket from his hand, sending it twenty feet away.
memories.memory_text: I felt Nico Carter strike me hard in the torso, and the the weathered jacket was ripped from my hand, flying away into the snow.

grounded_facts: A the weathered jacket duel erupts between Carson Nolan and Nico Carter, later joined by Owen Finch, in a forest on Eastgate School during the night.
memories.memory_text: I stood with Owen Finch against Nico Carter in the forest, ignited the weathered jacket, and fought him—blocking his strikes, even landing a hit on his arm, but he overwhelmed me and knocked the the weathered jacket from my hand.

grounded_facts: Owen Finch reaches out with the Force at the same time as Nico Carter to claim the weathered jacket, and it flies to her instead.
memories.memory_text: I saw Owen Finch reach out with the Force at the same time as Nico Carter, and I couldn't believe it when the the weathered jacket flew past him and landed in her hand.

grounded_facts: Owen Finch successfully calls the weathered jacket to her hand through the Force and ignites it, marking her first use of the weapon.
memories.memory_text: I watched Owen Finch ignite the weathered jacket for the first time, and I felt a surge of hope seeing her stand there with it blazing in her hands.

grounded_facts: Owen Finch cries while holding Carson Nolan, expressing grief and affection for him despite having just met.
memories.memory_text: I remember Owen Finch holding me, crying and expressing grief as she thought I was gone, even though we had just met.

grounded_facts: The the silver notebook emerges from the newly-formed canyon, illuminating Owen Finch and offering hope of rescue.
memories.memory_text: I saw the the silver notebook emerge from the canyon, its lights cutting through the dust and shining on Owen Finch, and in that moment I felt a surge of hope—we weren't stranded anymore.

grounded_facts: Cameron Sinclair roars from the the silver notebook to alert Owen Finch and Carson Nolan of their rescue.
memories.memory_text: I heard Cameron Sinclair roar from the silver notebook, a loud, unmistakable call that told me he was there for us, that we were being rescued, and that we weren't alone out here.

grounded_facts: Cameron Sinclair physically brings Carson Nolan into the the silver notebook after exiting the ship himself.
memories.memory_text: I remember Cameron Sinclair carrying me up the ramp into the silver notebook while Owen Finch hurried alongside us.

grounded_facts: Carson Nolan is brought inside the silver notebook by Cameron Sinclair, indicating he is unable to move on his own.
memories.memory_text: I was carried inside the silver notebook by Cameron Sinclair, so I must have been too weak to walk on my own.

grounded_facts: Carson Nolan is carried off the silver notebook by Cameron Sinclair and received by medical personnel who confirm he has a heartbeat, indicating he is alive but injured.
memories.memory_text: I was carried off the silver notebook by Cameron Sinclair, and I remember hearing a voice say, 'He's hurt. We've got a heartbeat,' as medical personnel took me in.

grounded_facts: the silver notebook lands at Cedar Ridge Academy base, marking the arrival of Owen Finch, Carson Nolan, Cameron Sinclair, and the glass key, followed by medical response and emotional reunions.
memories.memory_text: I remember the silver notebook landing at Cedar Ridge Academy base, and though I was barely conscious, I could hear the crowds cheering as we arrived.

grounded_facts: Owen Finch tells Carson Nolan she believes they will meet again and thanks him, showing emotional support and connection.
memories.memory_text: I was told that we'll see each other again and thanked, though I don't remember it clearly—I was unconscious at the time.

memories.memory_text: I was screaming, just yelling in pure adrenaline after that shot — I couldn’t believe we pulled it off. Then I asked Logan Ellison his name, and he turned to me, confused by mine.
He said he wouldn’t use that number on me — called me 'Carson Nolan' instead. When he said it, I smiled without meaning to, and when I said it back, it felt real. Like it was actually me.
I woke up in the sand, heart pounding, and saw smoke rising over the dunes—I started running, calling Logan Ellison’s name, scrambling over the dune, desperate to find him.

I thought I saw Logan Ellison’s arm in the wreckage, but it was just his jacket—I tried to get closer, but the heat and smoke drove me back, and then the fighter started sinking, pulling itself into the sand like quicksand.

I walked across the dunes, pulling off my Spencer Cavendish gear piece by piece, feeling the heat on my skin for the first time without that helmet—Logan Ellison’s jacket over my head kept the sun out, but it was his name I kept thinking.
I grabbed Jonah Carter’s dome, shouting over the blaster fire, 'Come on, Jonah Carter!'—we had to keep moving or we were dead.
I reached for Owen Finch’s hand to pull her along, but she yanked it back—'I know how to run without you holding my hand!'—and suddenly I was the one following her.
I couldn't believe Owen Finch thought she could fly that quad-jumper — 'You?!' — and when I saw the silver notebook, I thought it was hopeless, just junk.
The quad-jumper exploded right in front of us — one second we had a chance, the next it was gone — and I saw Owen Finch make the call to go back for the silver notebook.

I remember shouting at Owen Finch to stay low—my voice cracking—because I knew the Northstar Collective’s tracking systems could lock onto us if we flew straight and high. Then I saw her let go of the yoke, the ship tilting, and I thought we were done.
I couldn't get the gun controls to respond—switches flicking, the chair spinning weird, everything felt backwards. I yelled that it wasn't easy back here either.
I finally got the guns to fire—I saw the blast streak out and hit back at the the brass jacket. For a second, I actually thought we might make it.
I saw the the brass jacket right in my sights after Owen Finch flipped the silver notebook—my hands were steady as I fired and watched it explode.

I was still buzzing from the fight, and Owen Finch came running up, laughing, saying I was amazing — I couldn’t believe someone was looking at me like that, like I was actually good at something worth proud of.

She smiled and said my name — 'Carson Nolan' — and for a second I felt real, but then I remembered: I lied to her. Jonah Carter knew it too. I didn’t get to say anything, but the guilt hit hard, right before the steam burst from the floor.

I knelt down to Jonah Carter, heart pounding, and whispered that I wasn’t with Cedar Ridge Academy—just trying to get away from the Northstar Collective—and begged him to tell us where the base was, like it was some kind of deal we could make.
When Owen Finch said she had to go back to Fairview Street, I just exploded—'BACK TO JAK--?!'—it came out loud and raw, like I couldn’t believe anyone would ever want to return to that place.
I remember sitting in the Maplewood Heights, heart pounding, realizing the Northstar Collective was after us — and then it hit me, the gas system Owen Finch had fixed... maybe she could undo it.

I asked Owen Adler if he was really hauling Adrian Vaughn on this freighter, and when he said yes, my stomach dropped—I’d only heard rumors about those things, and now we’re stuck on a ship with them.

I was asking Owen Adler where he was keeping the Adrian Vaughn, and then—bam—this grotesque giant tongue slams into the container window right behind me. I froze. I’d never seen anything like that before.
I saw the Adrian Vaughn tearing into those Westfield Academy members, and when Owen Finch asked what they looked like, all I could do was say, 'They look like that,' before yanking her away.
I was pulling Owen Finch down the corridor, yelling 'This way!' when she hesitated, and then—something grabbed me, yanked me off my feet, and dragged me around the corner before I could even react.
It had me — the tentacle was wrapped around my leg, and I couldn't break free until the blast door came down and severed it. I was shaking, trying to kick the thing off me.
I saw Owen Finch running toward me, alive and smiling — I couldn't believe we both made it. Then we just ran, together, down the corridor toward the silver notebook.

I remember Owen Adler shouting at me to take care of Cameron Sinclair as we ran for the silver notebook, and feeling that weight hit me—Cameron Sinclair was hurt, screaming in pain, and I had to get him to safety.

I was trying to wrap Cameron Sinclair's shoulder, but he was howling and thrashing—every time I got close, he roared like he was going to tear me apart. I kept yelling for him to hold still, but I didn't know if I could even help him without getting killed.
I was trying to bandage Cameron Sinclair, but he grabbed me by the collar and roared in my face—after everything, I still had to help him, even though he almost killed me six times.
I told Owen Adler I was a big deal in Cedar Ridge Academy, but when he just brushed it off and walked away, I couldn't shake the guilt—like I didn't even believe it myself.
I was getting on that freighter, finally getting away—then I heard that sound from the sky and turned back. The path of fire in the distance... I knew. They were here.
Graham Nolan thrust the the weathered jacket into my hands and told me to find Owen Finch—then the whole corridor shook like something was tearing the Harborview Warehouse apart.
I saw Nico Carter carrying Owen Finch into his shuttle—she was just limp in his arms, and I couldn’t move at first. My chest tightened like something inside me had cracked.
I ran toward the shuttle, screaming her name through the blasts and smoke, but it lifted off and I couldn’t catch it. I kept yelling—'No, no, no, no... Owen Finch!'—even as it disappeared.
Emery Everett took my hand and thanked me—she knew what I did, about renouncing the Northstar Collective and saving Logan Ellison. I wasn’t expecting that, not from her.
I told her Owen Finch was taken to Eastgate School—I had to get there fast. I didn’t care about anything else, not until she said I had to tell them everything first.

I looked at Sidney Hale pinned by Cameron Sinclair, blaster in my hand, and said, 'Not anymore. The name's Carson Nolan, and I'm in charge.' My voice didn't shake, but I felt it—this was the moment I stopped being who they made me.

memories.memory_text: I boarded the silver notebook, told Cameron Sinclair we were home, and asked where the others were. I found out Owen Finch stole it from Jamie Monroe, who got it from others who took it from me. I said I was taking it back.

I heard the girl say my name like it meant something—'You're Owen Adler?'—and then she rattled off the Kessel Run like it was legend. I didn't know what to do with that, so I just said I used to be, but I felt it—the weight of being recognized, not just as a smuggler, but as someone they'd heard stories about.
I heard that the glass key was carrying a map to Owen Reeves, and when the kid said I knew him... it stopped me cold. I turned and said, 'Yeah, I knew him. I knew Owen Reeves.'
I tried to play it cool with Kendall Brooks, smiling and saying 'Good to see you,' but the second he cocked that weapon and said 'It's over for you,' I knew this wasn't about deals anymore.
I told the Westfield Academy I always delivered what I promised, and when they called me out—'Twice!'—I actually had to ask which time, and that's when I knew: my luck had finally run out.
I punched that Crown Hill Press thug hard—felt his jaw crack under my fist—and threw him straight into the Adrian Vaughn’s path so we could keep moving.
I heard Cameron Sinclair roar in pain after he got hit—saw him go down hard. I had to check on him, even for a second, before grabbing his bowcaster.
I snatched Cameron Sinclair's bowcaster and blasted the door controls—felt the kick of it in my hands. That thing packed a punch, but we had to keep moving.

I told Owen Finch to angle the shields while I worked the controls, trying to keep the silver notebook steady as that Adrian Vaughn’s giant mouth tore at the windshield—I could feel the ship shudder with every hit.

I pushed the silver notebook into lightspeed from inside the hangar, telling Owen Finch I never ask if it’s possible until after I’ve done it—then that monster slammed into the Maplewood Heights glass.
Jordan Hale reported to the Northstar Collective that I have the the glass key they want aboard the Maplewood Heights.

I shouted 'Electrical overload!' and Owen Finch immediately responded she could fix it—her voice cut through the alarms, calm but urgent, and for a second I felt like we might actually hold this ship together.

When I yelled about the coolant leak, Owen Finch suggested transferring auxiliary power to the secondary tank—I didn't hesitate, just confirmed it and moved—'Secondary tank, I got it!'—trusting her call under fire.
I said if they hurt Cameron Sinclair, they'd have to deal with me.

I told Carson Nolan he did good—meant it too, even if it felt awkward saying it. Kid had nerve, and after seeing him fumble with that holochess set, I knew he wasn’t just some Spencer Cavendish running scared.

I stood there, watching that hologram fill the room, and realized I wasn’t just telling them about Owen Reeves—I was admitting it to myself. The Force, the Jedi… I used to call it all mumbo-jumbo. But standing there, I said it out loud: it’s true.
I handed Carson Nolan a blaster after he called me 'Owen Adler' and started worrying about targets on his back—I told him women always figure out the truth, then walked off.
I offered Owen Finch a spot as second mate on the silver notebook, watching her hold that blaster like she already knew what it meant to survive out here.
I told Graham Nolan that Emery Everett doesn't want to see me—just saying it made the weight come back, like I've been carrying it the whole time.
I remember scanning the crowd, my gut tightening as I asked, 'Where's Owen Finch?'—everything else burning in the sky could wait.
I saw that the weathered jacket in Graham Nolan’s hands and something in me just tightened—where did she get that? It wasn’t just a weapon, I knew it meant something bigger, something old.

I saw Carson Nolan go down, that mace-wielding Spencer Cavendish raising his weapon to finish him—I didn’t think, just fired. The shot dropped the trooper clean, and I pulled Carson Nolan up, asking if he was okay. He looked at me like I’d come out of nowhere.

Just as they were marching us away, I heard it—the roar of X-wings. I turned and saw them skimming the lake, Cedar Ridge Academy pouring in. That black-marked X-wing diving down to hit the the brass jacket—it hit me then: we weren’t done yet.
I grabbed the blaster and fired—no time to think, just move, with Cameron Sinclair at my side and that kid Carson Nolan yelling like we’d already won.
I saw him—Nico Carter—carrying Owen Finch into that shuttle, and for a second, everything stopped. My own son… gone to them.
I looked at Emery Everett after all those years and the first thing I said was about her hair—'You changed your hair'—and she shot back, 'Same jacket.'
After Cameron Sinclair hugged her and walked on, I told her quietly, 'I saw him. Emery Everett, I saw our son. He was here,' and I could feel Graham Nolan watching through the smoke.
I saw the X-wings getting torn apart up there, and I knew we couldn't just run. I told Carson Nolan we had to use Cameron Sinclair's explosives—my friend and I have been through worse than this.
I heard Emery Everett’s voice in my head, telling me not to give up on him—so I stepped out onto the catwalk, called his name. Nico Carter.
He took off the mask. I saw his face—my son’s face—and something inside me jolted. I told him the truth: 'My son is alive.'
I reached out to him, ready to help my son come back—then the light went out, and I felt the blade go through me.

memories.memory_text: I stood there, stomach tight with hunger, staring at Unkar as he offered sixty portions for Jonah Carter—enough food to last weeks—but when I saw the the glass key looking up at me, beeping in fear, I heard myself say he wasn’t for sale.

I kicked and hit those thugs, knocked over the metal urns in the struggle—felt the sand under my hands when one of them fell. When I pulled the sack off Jonah Carter, I saw Carson Nolan staring, and something in his look made me tense up.

I charged at Carson Nolan with my quarterstaff—he ran, but I cut him off and slammed him down. When I demanded, 'What's your hurry, thief?' he looked shocked, and then Jonah Carter zapped him right there.
I saw the quad-jumper and shouted that we might make it in that ship — Carson Nolan didn’t think I could fly, but I told him we already had a pilot.
The quad-jumper exploded when the the brass jacket hit it — I stopped, turned right toward the camera, and said the garbage would do, meaning that wreck we were running to — the silver notebook.
I told him my name—'I'm Owen Finch'—and it felt like the first time I'd offered anything real to someone in a long time.
Steam burst under the grating and I shouted 'Help me with this!'—we pulled it up together, me and Carson Nolan, without thinking, like we already knew how to work as a team.

I had to shout over the blaring alarm and steam to get Carson Nolan to hand me the pilex driver while Jonah Carter hesitated about the base location — if I was flying them there, I needed to know we weren’t flying into a death trap.
Carson Nolan asked why I wanted to go back to Fairview Street and if I had a boyfriend, but I didn’t answer. When the power cut out, I had to keep working on the leak.
I looked up at Owen Adler with my hands raised, heart pounding, and said, 'I'm the pilot...'—then saw his doubt, but held my ground.
I stepped forward and told Owen Adler we needed his help — that Jonah Carter had to reach Cedar Ridge Academy right away, that it was urgent.
I remember asking Owen Adler what he was going to do with Jonah Carter, my voice tight with worry as the hatch opened beneath us and the others started moving.
I asked Owen Adler what he was going to do, unsure how words could stop whatever was coming—my hands tense at my sides, the memory of that slamming tentacle still fresh.
I turned the corner and saw those Westfield Academy members fighting something horrible—those writhing tentacles, the screaming—and I froze, covering my mouth, heart slamming in my chest.
Carson Nolan was right beside me, yelling to go this way—then suddenly he was yanked away, screaming, vanishing around the corner so fast I couldn't even reach him.
I called out for Carson Nolan—his name ripped out of me—after turning the corner and seeing he was gone, just... gone. The silence after his scream hit me like a wall.
I saw the control panel—monitors flashing, Carson Nolan on one screen, being dragged toward an open blast door. I slammed the button the second I saw the chance, felt it click under my hand.
Owen Adler shouted at me to close the door as we ran up the ramp—there was no time to think, just move.
I remember rushing past Owen Adler to Cameron Sinclair’s seat, knowing exactly what to do — Jamie Monroe’s fuel pump would stall us if we didn’t prime it first.
After hitting the controls, I told Owen Adler we weren’t going anywhere without priming the pump — then said he could use a co-pilot, claiming my place beside him before he could argue.
I hit the compressor switch—simple fix, but Owen Adler didn’t see it. The hyperdrive fired, and we jumped to lightspeed just in time.
I remember shouting over the alarms that I could fix the electrical overload, then telling Owen Adler to transfer auxiliary power to the secondary tank when he said the coolant was leaking.

I held the blaster in my hand, feeling its weight, and when Owen Adler asked if I wanted to be second mate on the silver notebook, I almost said yes—but I thought of Fairview Street, of waiting for my family, and told him I'd already been away too long.

I asked, 'What fight?'—and Graham Nolan answered that it was the only fight, against the dark side, that it had been the Sith, the Empire, and now the Northstar Collective. Her voice was heavy, like she’d seen it all before and knew how bad it could get.

I saw Graham Nolan crawl across the table, knocking over food, staring at Carson Nolan with huge eyes through her goggles—something changed in her face, like she recognized something deep in him, and I didn’t know what it meant, but it felt like the air had shifted.
I heard a child crying and felt a deep vibration pulling me toward that door, like it was calling my name, and I didn’t understand why I was moving but I couldn’t stop.

I touched the the weathered jacket and suddenly I was somewhere else—Cloud City, the hallway from the stories—then the ground shifted and I was in a field, watching a burning temple, Spencer Everett, and a man with a mechanical hand kneeling in the rain.

I saw myself as a child on Fairview Street, screaming for the ship to come back, Jamie Monroe dragging me away—then suddenly I was in frozen woods, breath visible, and Nico Carter appeared from behind a tree, making me scream and fall.
I couldn't move—his hand on my face, tearing into my mind, and I felt the map being pulled from me like blood from a wound. When he said they had what they needed, I just... fell.

I focused on the guard, my voice steady despite the fear—'You will remove these restraints. And leave this cell, with the door open.' My heart pounded as he moved toward me, rifle in hand, and I didn't know if he was going to free me or crush me.
